explainer.counted: People displaced inside Sudan by conflict or violence on 31 December 2025, as estimated by IDMC.
explainer.type: A stock: people present at the end of the year, not the number who arrived that year.
explainer.not_included: People displaced by disasters (counted separately) and people who crossed a border.
explainer.reliability: Most IDMC figures are estimates built from several sources (governments, UN agencies, media).

explainer.counted: People displaced inside Sudan by conflict or violence on 31 December 2025, as reported to UNHCR (people UNHCR protects or assists).
explainer.type: A stock: people present at the end of the year, not the number who arrived that year.
explainer.not_included: IDPs displaced by disasters, and IDPs UNHCR does not protect or assist.
explainer.reliability: Reported to UNHCR, often by the host government. The data does not say, row by row, whether a figure is a government count, a registration count or an estimate.

explainer.counted: Times people were newly forced to move inside Sudan by conflict and violence during 2025, as estimated by IDMC. Counts movements, not people.
explainer.type: A flow: counted during the year, not a year-end total.
explainer.not_included: People displaced earlier who are still displaced (that is the stock).
explainer.reliability: Most IDMC figures are estimates built from several sources (governments, UN agencies, media).

limitations.text: UNHCR and IDMC give the same figure in 2023 and 2024
limitations.detail: The two sources report identical numbers for these years, so they are likely based on the same underlying count. They are still shown side by side, never added.
IDMC's new displacements count each forced move, so one person displaced twice counts twice. Compare them with year-end totals with care.
South Sudan's independence changed the territory counted as Sudan.
The figure went from {n0} to {n1} in one year. The source data doesn't say why; a change in counting can look like real movement.
